Senses.Explanation: The compound functions as "as I knew," "sure enough," or "I knew it." It occurs 371 times in 147 allowlisted texts. Its frequent Chan setting is the public interview, where one turn marks the speaker's prior expectation or recognition of the other. One master says, "as I knew, you are at a loss" (情知汝罔措), and cuts off the monk as he is about to continue. Another hears that a visitor has come from Huangbo and says, "as I knew, you had been to see an adept" (情知你見作家來). Later case commentary uses the same construction to anticipate the reader: "as I knew, you misconstrue it here" (情知你向者裏錯會). The corpus also records the compact reply "I knew it" (情知), followed by the master's verdict, "a fierce tiger does not eat meat lying down" (猛虎不食伏肉). These grammatical forms attest recognition or expectation; they do not name a separate faculty of “feeling-knowledge.”
Senses.Note: Several early exchanges recur in multiple lamp compilations. Repeated recensions establish transmission, but the curated set does not count each recension as an independent event.
